plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, including pompon, spider, and decorative types. Prized in gardens and floristry, it thrives in the cool, short days of late autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; native to East Asia (China and Japan)
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are a symbol of the Japanese Imperial family, and the Chrysanthemum Throne is named after the flower. They are short-day plants, so they flower only as nights lengthen.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful tree covered in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, often before the fern-like leaves fully emerge. In late spring it lines streets with a carpet of fallen blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa, and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacarandas earn it the nickname 'Jacaranda City.' In Australia, a local tradition says that if a jacaranda blossom falls on your head, you will pass your exams.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that blooms in autumn, earlier than the common camellia. It bears fragrant, delicate, often single or semi-double flowers with prominent golden stamens, and it brightens gardens as other plants fade.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to Japan; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and temperate Asia
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis, and its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, used in cooking and cosmetics in Japan and China.

plants.name: Aster novae-angliae
plants.description: A robust native wildflower of North American meadows and roadsides, producing masses of daisy-like flowers with yellow centers. It is among the last nectar sources of the year for migrating monarch butterflies and other pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to late autumn (August to November)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, in meadows, prairies, and wet fields
plants.funFact: The flower heads close up on cloudy days and at night, and the plant is a crucial fall fuel stop for monarch butterflies on their migration to Mexico.
